issues.description: The ray-sphere function is inconsistently declared and used across files: the header (ray_sphere_intersect.h) declares a function named check_sphere_hit(...) while the implementation defines ray_sphere_intersect(...) and main.cpp calls ray_sphere_intersect(...). This mismatch between the function declaration, definition, and usage will lead to compilation errors or undefined references and confuses students about which API to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration, definition and usage consistent. Either (a) change the header to declare bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float*, const float*, const float*, const float); or (b) rename the implementation and all call sites to check_sphere_hit with the same signature. Update comments to document the correct API so students implement/use the intended function name and signature.

issues.description: The template's header for the sphere intersection function declares it as check_sphere_hit(...) while the implementation and all call sites use the name ray_sphere_intersect(...). The solution repository uses ray_sphere_intersect(...) in the header. This mismatch between the declaration in the template header and the implementation/call sites (and the solution) creates a direct mapping/confusion for students and will likely cause compilation errors or uncertainty about which function to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template header (template_repository/example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h) rename the function declaration from check_sphere_hit(...) to ray_sphere_intersect(...) so it matches the implementation and the solution. Ensure the prototype signature matches: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius);
